title: A draining tank follows Torricelli's law exactly
rationale: Integrating dh/dt = -c_d a sqrt(2 g h)/A gives h(t) = (sqrt(h0) - c_d a sqrt(2g) t/(2A))^2, an exact solution with nothing fitted. This fixture exists because the port-Hamiltonian form of Torricelli's law is easy to get subtly wrong: requiring R grad_H to reproduce the rate of change of HEAD (not of volume) gives R = c_d a sqrt(2g/h)/(rho g A^2), and dropping the g under the radical or one factor of A yields a model that is dimensionally inconsistent (dh/dt in m^2.5) yet still produces a smooth, plausible decay curve. That exact error existed in a real implementation and no accuracy test caught it -- only dimensional analysis did. Here it shows up as a 157 percent error against the closed form. The horizon stops well before the tank empties, so this fixture tests the drain law alone, uncontaminated by the empty-tank boundary.

parameters._units: A, a in m^2; g in m/s^2; c_d dimensionless; rho in kg/m^3

checks.closed_form: h(t) = (sqrt(h0) - c_d a sqrt(2g) t / (2A))^2, exact for Torricelli discharge

derived_quantities.note: a model missing sqrt(g)/A gives 1.445 instead of 0.562
